points.title: Malware and payload
points.must: Malware = software designed to damage, disrupt or gain unauthorised access; payload = the harmful action it performs.

points.title: Virus vs worm vs Trojan
points.must: Virus needs a host file and user action; worm spreads by itself over a network; Trojan is disguised as useful software and installed by the user.

points.title: Other malware types
points.must: Spyware / keylogger, ransomware, adware, botnet bot, rootkit — how each works.

points.title: Problems caused by malware
points.must: For individuals (data and money loss, identity theft) and organisations / society (downtime, financial loss, reputation, critical infrastructure, DDoS).

points.title: Ransomware case
points.must: Phishing → files encrypted → ransom → downtime; restore from offline backup rather than paying; why paying is not recommended.

points.title: Countermeasures against malware
points.must: Anti-malware with updated signatures, firewall, updates, trusted sources only, no unknown attachments, limited user rights, offline backups.

points.title: Privacy policy
points.must: A legal document explaining what personal data is collected, why, how it is used, stored, protected and shared, and the user’s rights.

points.title: Personal data and consent
points.must: Personal data identifies a person (name, IIN, address, location, IP); consent is informed, clear agreement that can be withdrawn.

points.title: Contents of a privacy policy
points.must: At least six: data collected, purpose, sharing with third parties, storage time and place, security, cookies, user rights, children, contact / changes.

points.title: Why privacy policies are needed
points.must: Required by law (Kazakhstan Law on Personal Data, GDPR), informed consent, accountability, trust.

points.title: Problems with privacy policies
points.must: Long and legal language, take-it-or-leave-it, can change, do not guarantee security.

points.title: Reading a policy
points.must: A worked example extracting data collected, purpose, sharing, storage period and user rights from a short policy.
